newsitem.title: JAPAN: AT&T launches low-cost Internet service in Japan.
newsitem.headline: AT&T launches low-cost Internet service in Japan.

text.p: AT&T Corp. and 25 Japanese partners Thursday launched a low-cost Internet access service for individual users in Japan.

AT&T Jens Corp., a joint venture between AT&T and 25 Japanese firms, began offering Japanese users unlimited access to the Internet for a flat rate of 2,000 yen ($17) per month, after a one-time registration fee of 3,000 yen ($26).
The rates are lower than those of other such services in Japan, including Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.'s planned Open Computer Network.
Under the Open Computer Network, NTT will charge 2,300 yen ($20) per month for access to the Internet for up to 15 hours a month. The service is expected to start later this month.

AT&T, which launched an Internet access service for consumers in the United States in March, has signed up more than 425,000 U.S. customers since then and has become the second-biggest provider in the United States.
